### UTC Date & Time

[November 27, 2025, 14:00 UTC](https://savvytime.com/converter/utc/nov-27-2025/2pm)

### Agenda

- Fusaka
  - updates from testnets, mainnet shadow forks?
  - https://github.com/ethereum/pm/blob/master/Fusaka/fusaka-mainnet-plan.md
  - anything else?
- Glamsterdam
  - any devnet updates?
  - [call out for trustless payments discussion](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1812#issuecomment-3581152422)
  - continue fork scoping
    - 7805 (FOCIL)
    - 7688 (Forward compatible consensus data structures)
    - 8045 (Exclude slashed validators from proposing)
    - 8061 (Increase exit and consolidation churn)
    - 8062 (Add sweep withdrawal fee for 0x01 validators)
    - 8071 (Prevent using consolidations as withdrawals)
    - 8080 (Let exits use the consolidation queue)
- Heka / Bogotá
  - portmanteau: Boka?

All Core Devs - Consensus

90 minutes

bi-weekly

Assuming we aim for two upgrades a year.

**Minimum mainnet timeline from testnet releases** 
(based on https://github.com/ethereum/pm/blob/master/processes/protocol-upgrade.md)

| Event | Min days | Total elapsed |
|-------|------------|---------------|
| testnet release(s) |   | 0  |
| 1st testnet upgrade |  14 | 14 |
| 2nd testnet upgrade | 14 | 28 |
| mainnet date set | 2 | 30 |
| mainnet client releases | 7 | 37 |
| mainnet upgrade | 30 | 67|

_Completely hypothetical mainnet targets (for illustration purposes only)_
**Glamsterdam**: June 24, 2026, testnet release(s) required by April 18, 2026 (at the latest).
**Heka-Bogotá**: December 9, 2026, testnet release(s) required by October 3, 2026 (at the latest). 
*Note 2026 is a Devcon year

### Low priority

We need to come up with a list of [I-star names](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/i-star-name-for-consensus-layer-upgrade-after-heka/26717) for the upgrade after Heka.  For anyone into stars and naming.

Apparently [Heka is not in the IAU list of stars](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/h-star-name-for-consensus-layer-upgrade-after-glamsterdam/24298/10), but I assume it is too late to change as All Core Devs already decided.

i think most are aware conversation has been stirring around trustless payments and splitting them out of 7732.
i'm not convinced myself the next acdc is the right place for a big discussion between the conflicting perspectives.
i do think we should at least mention that some are pushing to create a more complete picture together and see what consensus is. so expect me to do that on this call. perhaps something like a minimal 5min would already suffice.

for a more full discussion, next epbs call is one natural moment to do that. if people are worried about delaying the fork perhaps sooner would be better. happy to take responsibility for organizing if desired. still talking to stokes about this.

I may not make the call due to a conflict, but I'd just like to publicly state [Obol](https://obol.org)'s support for [EIP7688](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7688) - Forward Compatible containers inclusion in Glamsterdam. We, as well as other teams in staking, have developed proof-based systems for asserting statements about the CL on the EL side. However we did not ship the feature to production, in part because we developed it in January this year, and it was broken in Electra due to a layout change. Breaking proof systems, requiring re-audits, and upgradeable contracts, are massive costs, risks, and downsides for Ethereum's decentralisation, and we hope this feature can be SFI'd for Glamsterdam to prevent this continuing, (and that the core devs put more focus on retaining eth's [declining decentralisation](https://x.com/robplust/status/1975872756647649325) in H-star with EIPs such as [FOCIL](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7805) and [Correlation penalties](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7716), but they're for a separate ACD :) ). Thanks!

Here's Lido's thoughts on PFId CL EIPs for Glamsterdam. # Summary **Support:** * [7688](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7688): Forward Compatible consensus data structures * [8045](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8045): Exclude slashed validators from proposing * [8068](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8068): Neutral effective balance design * [8071:](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8071) Prevent using consolidations as withdrawals OR [8080:](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8080) Let exits use the consolidation queue **Do not support:** * [8062](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8062): Add sweep withdrawal fee for 0x01 validators **FOCIL:** Move to Heka, given the workload of client teams on the headliners. # Rationale ## Support for Inclusion **[7688](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7688) - Forward Compatible consensus data structures**: Stabilizes Merkle indices in the Beacon state, preventing future upgrades from breaking proofs used by protocols relying on EIP-4788. This eliminates repeated rework, reduces operational risk, and future-proofs the rapidly growing ecosystem of staking, bridging, and ZK systems built on Beacon Chain data. **[8045](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8045) - Exclude slashed validators from proposing:** Natural improvement of Ethereum PoS, fixing a known unwanted feature. Moreover, it does not add much additional complexity, so shouldn’t delay shipping. **[8068](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8068) - Neutral effective balance design:** Fair improvement on the calculation of effective balance. Makes effective balance well defined and improves compounding of 0x02 validators, incentivizing switching from 0x01 to 0x02. **Fixing consolidation vs exit queue flaw ([8071](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8071) or [8080](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8080)):** In Pectra upgrade, a flaw introduced in Electra which allows surplus ETH (the delta of the amount and 2048) consolidated onto an 0x02 validator be withdrawn via the automatic sweep and bypass the exit queue via the consolidation queue. Our team identified this and reported to EIP-7251 authors. We support fixing this issue; currently, two alternatives are EIP 8071 and EIP 8080. We are actively reviewing the specs in order to make sure a final fix included in Glamsterdam is stable and covers all holes. ## Do not support **[8062](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8062) - Add sweep withdrawal fee for 0x01 validators:** This proposal introduces an additional fee that unfairly targets 0x01 validators and does not align with Ethereum’s decentralization goals, as explained below: **Context:** Lido contributors have already undergone months of work to support the gradual shift of the network to 0x02 validators. Lido V3’s stVaults, launching in late December, are 0x02 by default, and [contributors further have proposed for the of the majority of stake operated via Lido Core to be migrated to 0x02 validators by Q3/2026](https://research.lido.fi/t/future-of-the-curated-module-cmv2-landscape/10929) (starting in Q1/2026, when Curated Module v2 is aimed to be launched). 1. **It meaningfully changes economics for small stakers:** Many solo and home stakers rely on the automated sweep at the maximum effective balance as a predictable income stream. This suggested change effectively penalizes those who wish to retain a smaller validator (MAX_EB == 32) vs those who consolidate, but the two ways of running a validator are substantively different (compounded vs automatically withdrawn rewards). While the general intent to consolidate as much of the network is fully supported and laudable, the bulwark of the change should come from large node operators and protocols. The counter-argument that EL-triggered partial withdrawals are available is acknowledged, but it should be noted that there may be tax treatment differences depending on jurisdiction and also require an additional onchain actions (spending ETH on mainnet). 2. **It hurts trust-minimized bond-based permissionless staking:** Trust-minimized permissionless staking solutions (such as Lido Community Staking Module - CSM, Rocket Pool, and Stader) rely on 0x01 validators, using small fractional bond requirements. These solutions enable home stakers to participate with minimal barriers to entry, and have dramatically increased the number of node operators for whom staking from home is now accessible, effectively serving as Ethereum public goods. As creating application-layer mechanisms to reason about and manage bonding requirements for validators with effective balances between 32 and 2048 ETH is immensely complex and costly, the base assumption for most protocols is that either a sub-set of validators would be kept as 0x01 or custom MAX_EB ceilings would be introduced to allow for larger, but still manageable bond requirements. Lido contributors believe that CSM can grow to over 10% of Lido protocol stake in 2026. Although a version of CSM can also be created to support 0x02 validators, without custom ceilings it is too technically and operationally complex to develop an upgrade that dynamically manages bond requirements, thus a “tax” on 0x01 validators in the interim essentially makes it harder to maintain this public good. 3. **Unfair resource allocation:** The proposal also introduces asymmetry: while 0x02 validators can withdraw excess over MAX_EB without additional cost, 0x01 validators would face extra fees. This creates an unjustifiable bias against a non-obsolete class of validators. The network should allow a small portion of type 0x01 validators (by choice or necessity), without penalizing this option. # On FOCIL We support the FOCIL proposal and recognize its importance for Ethereum’s roadmap. However, based on the feedback we are getting from client teams, we came to the conclusion that including FOCIL in this upgrade would likely delay its rollout and also eliminate several other EIPs which provide valuable improvements At present, Ethereum’s censorship resistance is in a healthy state, with no indications of deterioration. Given the current workload of client teams and the inclusion of major items like ePBS and Block-Level Access Lists, we believe moving FOCIL to the H* upgrade would not meaningfully alter its impact and value, compared to targeting its inclusion in Glamsterdam. Excluding FOCIL at this stage also helps maintain a clear upgrade focus: Glamsterdam’s primary theme would remain scalability (through EIP-7732 block pipelining update and Block-Level Access Lists), while FOCIL could serve as the central feature of the following Heka upgrade, emphasizing on censorship resistance.

Not really a consensus related question, but we should consider working on making the engine ssz compatible. Maybe this is for a future call, but would like to open this box today, if we get some time in the end.
